plate-1-work.svg: I · Work — the one section drawn as an empty footprint: a component the board expects that is not fitted, because the year of paid work is off-repo. A 57.8M-row field-usage table, distilled from 1.6M Oracle Analytics query logs at Miami University. None of these numbers can be re-derived by a reader — the data belongs to Miami University and to a competition; this section is attested, not derived.
plate-2-jetpack.svg: II · jetpack — parallel gzip on JDK 25, drawn as the SIMD bus fanning into four deflate blocks stitched back to one gzip member: 422 against 66.2 MB per second single-threaded, 6.4 times, on an M1 Pro from a 3-fork JMH run. The against-self result is printed on the plate: the JDK's own Adler-32 intrinsic does 14.06 GB per second and is not beaten; the hand-vectorised checksum reaches 4.26, bit-identical to java.util.zip.
plate-3-glyph.svg: III · Glyph — SIMD kernels over a course-provided MNIST net, drawn as three register-lane bundles — NEON, AVX2, AVX-512 — converging on benchDot/256: 3.5× over the course baseline on the reference machine. The package that ships is WASM_SIMD128, 43,751 bytes, byte-identical to main and checked daily in CI. The against-self results are printed: the same flags run 10.7× slower on benchAxpy/128, below the size floor, and 97.01% is a training-time number — the test set that graded the net also picked its checkpoint.
